worksheets.explanation: We use "a" before a word that starts with a consonant SOUND, and "an" before a word that starts with a vowel SOUND. It is the sound that matters, not just the letter. For example: "honourable knight" starts with a consonant sound, so we say "a honourable knight". "European city" starts with a vowel sound, so we say "an European city". Some words break the usual pattern: "hour" starts with a silent letter, so we say "an hour". "Unicorn" starts with a "y" sound, so we say "a unicorn".
